### 1. Architecture Overview
Prometheus’ native histogram flows from in-memory generation to on-disk persistence and on-the-wire transport. The source of truth is `model/histogram/histogram.go`, which defines `Histogram` along with operations like copy, validation, and compaction (lines 35‑120). Histograms are produced both by the ingestion path (e.g., `util/convertnhcb/convertnhcb.go` converting classic buckets, lines 137‑200) and by test/data utilities (`tsdb/tsdbutil/histogram.go`, lines 21‑97). Once constructed, histograms are encoded into TSDB records via `tsdb/record/record.go` (`DecodeHistogram` at lines 495‑549 handles serialization round-trips) and chunk metadata via `tsdb/chunkenc/histogram_meta.go`, which stores schema, spans, and other layout data (lines 22‑174). Samples referencing histograms are routed through `tsdb/chunks/samples.go`, whose `Sample` interface exposes `H() *histogram.Histogram` for downstream consumers (lines 21‑90). Introducing a new required field on `Histogram` therefore affects every layer: struct definition, constructors, converters, encoders/decoders, and any code in other systems (e.g., Thanos, Mimir) that create literal histograms.

### 2. Detailed Analysis
#### Histogram Core Definition
- `model/histogram/histogram.go` defines the `Histogram` struct (lines 35‑80). Adding `CreatedTimestamp int64` here makes it a required field for all histogram literals. Related methods (`Copy`, compaction, iterators) already copy all struct fields explicitly; each will need to include the new field when cloning or transforming histograms to avoid losing the timestamp.

#### Generators and Test Utilities
- `tsdb/tsdbutil/histogram.go` contains helpers like `GenerateTestHistogram` and `GenerateTestCustomBucketsHistogram` that return histogram literals (lines 39‑83). Each literal must set the new `CreatedTimestamp`, otherwise callers compiling with Go will fail and runtime behavior (e.g., deterministic test fixtures) will no longer match the new contract.
- Gauge/test variants (`GenerateTestGaugeHistogram`, `GenerateTestHistograms`, etc.) call these helpers and therefore rely on the struct fields being complete.

#### Converters from Classic Histograms
- `util/convertnhcb/convertnhcb.go` builds `histogram.Histogram` instances inside `TempHistogram.convertToIntegerHistogram` (lines 168‑199). Converters must populate `CreatedTimestamp` (likely from the source sample timestamp) so that downstream storage (TSDB, remote write) has the new metadata. Without doing so, newly generated native histograms will have zero timestamps, defeating the purpose of the new required field.

#### WAL/Chunk Serialization
- `tsdb/record/record.go` encodes/decodes histograms via `EncodeHistogram`/`DecodeHistogram`. `DecodeHistogram` (lines 495‑549) currently reads fields sequentially; it must be extended to read/write the timestamp to keep WAL/snapshot compatibility. Any omission would cause mismatched binary formats and corrupted WAL playback once the struct changes.
- `tsdb/chunkenc/histogram_meta.go` is responsible for chunk layout encoding (lines 22‑174) and counter reset hints (lines 469‑491). Introducing a timestamp could require updating the chunk metadata header if the timestamp is stored alongside schema and zero-threshold, and ensuring the merge/insert logic keeps bucket data aligned while carrying the timestamp through chunk writes.

#### Sample Plumbing
- `tsdb/chunks/samples.go` defines the `Sample` interface and backing struct `sample` storing `*histogram.Histogram` (lines 26‑88). While it doesn’t construct literals, any copy or mutation must ensure `CreatedTimestamp` survives `Copy()` operations (`s.h.Copy()` at lines 79‑85 needs to inherit the new field via `Histogram.Copy()`).

#### External Consumers (Thanos, Mimir, etc.)
- Thanos/Mimir convert Prometheus histograms for remote storage (e.g., their own converters and protobufs). Any file that imports `github.com/prometheus/prometheus/model/histogram` and instantiates `Histogram` literals—highlighted by cross-repo search results (e.g., `pkg/storage/chunk/prometheus_chunk.go` in Mimir, `pkg/store/storepb/prompb/samples.go` in Thanos per `smart_search`)—must set the field. Otherwise, compilation will fail or the timestamp will default to zero, breaking contract expectations between Prometheus TSDB and downstream systems.

---

**Summary:** Adding `CreatedTimestamp int64` to `Histogram` is a pervasive change: update the struct definition, copy/utility methods, every constructor/generator (Prometheus core + downstream projects), and all serialization pathways (WAL, chunk encoding, remote write converters). Neglecting any of these files causes either compilation failures (missing struct field in literals) or runtime corruption (timestamp not encoded/decoded).
